title: Step-Down Club: Maintenance After the Max Dose
one_liner: A cheap maintenance membership that turns the majority of GLP-1 users who quit or plateau into a planned step-down and a monetizable restart.
customer: Adults 3-12 months into a cash-pay GLP-1 who have hit goal or are about to quit over cost (consumer pays); telehealths and pharmacies pay a bounty per verified restart.
problem: About one-third of non-diabetic obesity patients are still on therapy at 1 year. Stoppers regain roughly 4x faster than people who lost weight with behavior change, and ~60% of ex-users say they intend to restart. Every company optimizes for staying on the max dose, and nobody sells the middle path or owns the ex-user.
solution: At plateau, a physician-written protocol steps the user down to the lowest effective dose or a planned holiday. A connected scale plus waist and strength check-ins run on SMS. Pre-agreed regain triggers (e.g. +3% above nadir for 2 consecutive weeks) auto-route the user to the cheapest legitimate restart, such as a $149 pill program. Optional 'regain warranty' credit as an add-on.
why_now: SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN (Lancet, 2026) is the first RCT showing a reduced 5 mg tirzepatide dose kept about 70% of the weight loss (-16.6% vs -21.9% at max dose vs -9.9% on placebo). $149-$299 pills (Wegovy pill Jan 2026, Foundayo Apr 2026) make restart cheap. Telehealths are converging on the same price and now compete on acquisition cost.
revenue_model: $19-29/month membership, plus $75-150 partner bounty per verified restart or step-down conversion (a telehealth's first-fill CAC is est. $150-400), plus optional warranty add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Discontinuation is the modal outcome, not a failure mode. A restart is a lead worth more than the membership fee, so whoever owns the ex-user relationship owns the cheapest reacquisition channel in a market where every competitor sells the same drug at the same price.
first_30_days: Recruit 100 plateaued or ex-users from r/Zepbound, r/Semaglutide and Facebook groups. Have an obesity-medicine MD write the step-down and restart protocol. Run the check-ins on SMS with a BYO or $25 scale. Sign one telehealth or pharmacy partner for a per-restart bounty. Charge $19/month from day one.

title: CRA Continuity Kit for One-Person Vendors
one_liner: An outsourced EU Cyber Resilience Act desk that handles the 24h/72h/14-day vulnerability reporting clock and keeps a signed 10-year release vault with a dead-man's-switch escrow, built for micro-vendors with no security team.
customer: Solo and micro hardware, firmware, app and SaaS vendors that sell into the EU, such as ESP32 and Raspberry Pi based device makers on Tindie or Crowd Supply, small GmbHs, and indie app publishers. There is no size exemption. They pay EUR 79-399/month per product.
problem: CRA Article 14 reporting began 11 September 2026: a 24-hour early warning, a 72-hour notification and a 14-day final report via ENISA's Single Reporting Platform, with fines up to EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. A one-person German GmbH selling firmware asks how to comply given CE marking, a technical file, 'every security update you ship has to stay available for 10 years' and no size threshold. Maintainers are already bailing out: the croniter fork was archived citing the CRA.
solution: A subscription that provides (1) a named on-call reporting desk that prepares and files the early warning, notification and final report on the vendor's delegated authority against a pre-agreed playbook; (2) SBOM generation and continuous vulnerability watch tied to the customer's release artifacts, to detect an 'actively exploited' trigger; (3) an immutable, signed release vault holding every shipped update for 10+ years, with a dead-man's-switch: if the vendor stops responding or dissolves, the firmware source and update artifacts are released to customers or a nominated steward; (4) a fixed-price 'CRA readiness sprint' that produces the technical-file skeleton and declaration-of-conformity scaffolding.
why_now: The reporting obligation went live 11 September 2026, so this is a forced-spend deadline, not a forecast. Full obligations follow in December 2027. Legal commentators say many still associate the CRA only with consumer IoT and are unprepared.
revenue_model: EUR 1,500 fixed-price readiness sprint, then EUR 79-399/month per product for the reporting retainer and vault, tiered by product count and risk class. Optional per-incident filing fee. Channel deals with device marketplaces and Linux/embedded distributors.
non_obvious_insight: The gap is not compliance dashboards (the Ask HN thread already lists Vulert, ReARM and the ORC WG hub) but staffed responsiveness and durable custody: a solo founder cannot staff a 24-hour clock or credibly promise 10 years of availability. A dead-man's-switch vault turns the founder's bus-factor into a compliance asset. Escrow at end of life is a recurring HN demand, e.g. 'When you release a product, you should be required to put the source code in escrow, so it can be released at EoL' https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44531176, and vendors ask for escrow tooling https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46402528. Evidence of demand: one-person GmbH asking for help https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49520688; obligations and fines https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/09/11/eus-cyber-resilience-act-starts-the-24-hour-vulnerability-clock/5295821; croniter archived https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43168860.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 design partners from the Open Regulatory Compliance WG CRA hub, Torizon CRA summit attendees, and Tindie/Crowd Supply sellers, plus the author of the Ask HN thread. Sell the EUR 1,500 sprint with a written 24h playbook and SBOM pipeline for their repos. Stand up the vault on object-lock storage with signed manifests and a heartbeat check-in. Have a CRA-literate lawyer review the delegation-of-filing template. Convert sprint customers to the retainer.

title: Ear-Coach for Early-Ed Teachers, Paid by QRIS
one_liner: Classroom-audio analysis that scores teacher-child interactions the way trained CLASS observers do and coaches staff weekly, sold to centers as a path to higher state quality-rating tiers and higher reimbursement.
customer: Directors and owners of centers and small chains (5-50 sites) in states with tiered-reimbursement QRIS programs. Also QRIS coaching contractors and Head Start grantees.
problem: Insiders picture AI in early education as child-facing. The real bottleneck is the adult: the average worker earns $33,140, turnover is high and coaching is sporadic. Quality-rating tiers drive subsidy-rate bonuses, but observation-based scoring needs scarce, costly trained observers, so centers stay stuck at low stars.
solution: Opt-in classroom audio pods or teacher-worn mics with on-device diarization and transcription (no child audio retained). They score serve-and-return turns, open-ended questions, language richness and tone. Each teacher gets a 3-minute weekly micro-coaching note on their phone, and directors get a mock-CLASS 'star readiness' report before official visits.
why_now: On-device diarization and transcription are cheap and good enough. New tax credits and subsidy money (45F at 40-50%, DCFSA to $7,500) are landing in centers in 2026. Child-facing AI is drawing lawsuits, while teacher-facing AI avoids that liability.
revenue_model: $40-80 per classroom per month, plus an optional success fee (a share of the reimbursement uplift) when the center's tier rises.
non_obvious_insight: Quality is a lever on price, since higher-tier centers earn higher reimbursement, so coaching can be sold as revenue rather than a cost. Putting AI in the adult's ear sidesteps the child-AI liability wave entirely.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 centers in a state that pays tier bonuses. Record consented lessons on phones and run open-source diarization. Have two ex-CLASS observers score 20 clips to validate the model's ratings. Sell a $500 'star readiness audit' per center, then convert to a monthly plan.

title: Vendor-neutral body-cam redaction bureau with fee pass-through
one_liner: A CJIS-cleared remote team that returns double-reviewed redacted police video priced per minute below the fee small cities already charge requesters, so the bureau funds itself.
customer: Small police departments and sheriff's offices (roughly 5-60 sworn officers) with records backlogs, and the city clerks and attorneys who carry the liability. They pay $0.40-0.60 per video minute plus a small monthly minimum.
problem: Small agencies do not have redaction staff. Elko, NV's police chief described about a year of catching up on redaction requests with no full-time redaction team and approved a five-year Axon extension of about $91,200 a year. White Salmon, WA has only two trained employees and set a $0.84-per-minute redaction fee (4-1 vote, April 15, 2026) while the chief said he 'cannot readily add a second-review step for all releases' because of limited trained staff and high request volume. A councilor dissented, arguing that sensitive footage such as juveniles needs more than one reviewer. Phoenix has nearly 40,000 pending public-records requests and raised commercial fees to pay for staff. AI-generated request floods (Somerset County, PA saw dozens a day) make it worse.
solution: A regional redaction bureau. Departments send only the clips requested (through share links from Axon, Motorola/WatchGuard, Getac and Wolfcom or others) and get back redacted video plus a redaction log within 5 business days. Automated face, plate and audio detection does the first pass. Then two trained human reviewers sign off, with a state-specific checklist (juveniles, victims, medical, informants). The bureau also sells 'backlog amnesty sprints' at a flat rate to clear a year-old queue. Vendor neutrality is the selling point, since Axon's automated redaction only helps agencies inside its ecosystem and still requires manual verification.
why_now: Body camera adoption is nearly universal after 2025-2026 contract cycles (Elko, Plainview, Crescent City, Carlsbad, Kasson approvals), public-records volume is up, and states are formalizing per-minute cost recovery. Councils are now adopting the fee schedules that make a pass-through model possible.
revenue_model: Per-minute fee ($0.40-0.60) billed to the agency, which recovers most or all of it from requesters at its own per-minute fee (White Salmon: $0.84); monthly minimum of $250; flat-rate backlog sprints of $5k-20k.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not blurring speed, it is a defensible second review on sensitive content, which small departments cannot staff. The fee schedule councils are adopting is derived from a cost-of-service study, so the department can pass the bureau's cost straight through; the bureau's margin lies between its price and the city's published fee. CJIS clearance and background checks form the moat that keeps generic video-AI startups out. Evidence: Elko's year-long backlog (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/7804457/nevada/elko-county/elko-city/elko-approves-five-year-axon-contract-for-body-cameras-and-redaction-software-to-clear-backlog); White Salmon's two trained employees, the $0.84/minute fee and the second-review dissent (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/8492326/washington/klickitat-county/white-salmon/council-updates-public-records-policy-approves-084-per-minute-body-camera-redaction-fee-over-staff-objections); Phoenix's roughly 40,000 pending requests (https://www.kjzz.org/politics/2026-09-24/commercial-public-records-requests-prices-have-gone-up-in-phoenix-in-effort-to-hire-more-staff).
first_30_days: Pick one state, such as Washington, with strong public-records laws and many small departments. Sign the CJIS security addendum with 2 agencies and have all reviewers fingerprint-cleared. Find 15 departments with a visible backlog in recent council minutes and offer a flat 'backlog amnesty sprint' on their first 500 minutes at $0.45/min. Turn the state's checklist into a review template and deliver the first 3 jobs within the month.

title: Funeral Committee Escrow and Fixed-Price Vendor Network
one_liner: A per-funeral M-Pesa vault where contributions can only be released to pre-priced vendors with two-of-three committee approvals, ending the 'where did the burial money go' fights.
customer: The family and burial committee (treasurer, chair, village elder, workplace welfare group) organising a rural funeral, usually with a Nairobi or diaspora fundraising arm. Vendors (tent and chair hire, caterers, coffin makers, embalmers, hearse and PA operators) are the second paying side.
problem: A rural funeral is often a family's biggest single cash event, drawing hundreds of mourners and costing multiples of a year's farm income. It is run on WhatsApp groups and an exercise book. Treasurer fraud and 'the money vanished' accusations are common and can split families for years. Vendors quote inflated prices to grieving families who cannot shop around, mortuary storage fees accrue daily so decisions are rushed, and families often sell land, borrow against coop shares or take mobile loans to close the gap. Existing crowdfunding tools collect money but do nothing about how it is spent.
solution: Each funeral gets a dynamic M-Pesa paybill account and a WhatsApp bot (English, Swahili, Sheng). The committee picks from fixed-price packages (basic, standard, large) with vendor prices published. Every payout to a vendor till needs two of three designated approvers by USSD PIN, and a live ledger is visible to all contributors. The bot also handles pledge tracking, reminders in the Nairobi and home committees, the mortuary and transport schedule, and a post-funeral accounting statement. Money sits in a licensed payment provider's trust account, not on the startup's balance sheet.
why_now: M-Pesa paybill, till and B2B payout APIs are mature enough to make programmable escrow cheap, and the WhatsApp Business API is inexpensive. LLMs now let a bot handle Swahili and Sheng committee chatter. The post-2023 cost-of-living squeeze makes families more sensitive to funeral overspending and to selling land to pay for it. Funeral crowdfunding has trained diaspora and urban Kenyans to give online, but nobody controls the spend side.
revenue_model: About 2-3% fee on money flowing through the vault plus negotiated vendor margins or referral commissions of roughly 8-12% on vendor spend. Later upsells are funeral cover (partnered with a licensed insurer), memorial pages, and body-transport routing between Nairobi and up-country.
non_obvious_insight: Money that is locked to named vendors is welcome, not resented: it protects the treasurer from the 'sharing tax' of relatives and neighbours asking for cash, and from accusations. In effect the product sells social protection, not payments. Funerals are also where families mortgage their long-term farm assets, so reducing funeral overspend is a farm-resilience product that VCs would never classify as agtech.
first_30_days: Recruit 8-10 vendors (tents, catering, coffins, hearse) along one corridor such as Nairobi to Murang'a or Nyeri and agree fixed package prices. Onboard the first 5 funerals by offering free setup through church welfare groups, alumni groups and your own contacts, using a manual approval flow on top of an existing paybill provider. Charge the fee only after a funeral closes with a clean statement, and use those statements as proof for the next 50.

title: 911 Dispatch Layer for Autonomous Fleets
one_liner: A RapidSOS-style shared layer inside police and fire dispatch tools that lets first responders instantly direct, reach and cite any autonomous vehicle, truck, delivery robot or drone fleet.
customer: Autonomous fleets pay per vehicle (Zoox, May Mobility, Avride, Beep, Gatik, Kodiak, Bot Auto, sidewalk-robot and drone operators). It is free to 911 centers and agencies.
problem: NHTSA sent a first-responder letter on Jul 8, 2026, and fleets rely on small remote-assistance desks (Waymo has about 70 agents on shift, with two centers in the Philippines). Every fleet has its own phone number and process, and driverless trucks have no one to talk to an inspector, since CVSA enhanced-inspection clearance lasts 24 hours and needs a trained inspector. State rules (Texas SB 2807 and California AB 1777, in effect from July 2026, verify) require emergency plans and fast compliance with geofence directives. Dispatchers have about 40 seconds and no unified tool.
solution: An add-in for dispatch systems (plus SMS and web fallback) and a fleet-side API providing geofence and closure directives with acknowledgment and a timestamped compliance receipt for the city. It also gives one-tap lookup by plate, VIN or fleet ID to a live human on that fleet's ops desk, intake and routing of 'notice of noncompliance' citations, a driverless-truck inspection scheduling module, and audit logs for regulators, with responder training cards and drills.
why_now: The state laws just took effect, fleets are multiplying (Waymo across 10-14 metros, Zoox charging fares, Tesla unsupervised in Texas and Florida, Aurora at 200 driverless trucks), and NHTSA is now actively engaging. Prior compliance tools (PrePass/Kodiak) cover only Texas and Louisiana.
revenue_model: $10-25 per vehicle per month plus a $25-60k onboarding fee per fleet, with optional municipal modules for citation processing and drills.
non_obvious_insight: The legal burden lands on fleets, but the user is a dispatcher with seconds, so you win by embedding in tools police already use and giving it away to agencies, as RapidSOS did. Fleets will pay because one standard is cheaper than hundreds of city-by-city integrations.
first_30_days: Interview 20 dispatchers and fire chiefs in Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta. Build a simple web and SMS directive-and-ack tool. Sign one mid-size fleet to a 90-day paid pilot and join the APCO/NENA standards working groups.

title: Orphan Lien Clearance Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A flat-fee curative service that proves dead solar fixture filings and other zombie liens are dead (or gets them released) so home closings stop stalling.
customer: Independent title and escrow agencies and real estate attorneys in high-solar states (AZ, CA, FL, TX, NJ, NC, NV, CO), billed per file and usually paid by the seller at closing. Listing agents in solar-heavy markets are a second channel.
problem: Sunnova filed Chapter 11 in June 2025 (500,000+ customers), Mosaic and PosiGen followed, and the residential solar credit ended for 2026 installs, so thousands of homes carry UCC-1 fixture filings and recorded solar-lease notices held by dead, merged or reassigned entities. Title examiners flag every one. Agents can't tell who holds the debt now, whether the filing is even still legally effective, or how to get a termination, so closings slip days or weeks. The people currently serving this are consumer SEO and lead-gen sites, not the title agents who actually need it solved on a deadline.
solution: Per-file lien autopsy delivered in 48 hours. (1) Pull the recorded instrument and any continuation or termination filings from the county index and the Secretary of State. (2) Compute lapse under UCC 9-515 (five years unless continued in the six-month window). (3) Trace the assignment and servicer chain through bankruptcy dockets and servicer notices. (4) Deliver either an underwriter-ready 'lapsed, no exception' memo, or a payoff/estoppel request plus a pre-drafted termination (UCC-3, or debtor-filed termination where the statute allows) recorded in that county's required format. Recorded memoranda of lease, which do not lapse, get a release workflow instead. Later expand the same engine to satisfied-but-never-released mortgages, expired judgment liens, dead PACE liens and resurfaced zombie second mortgages.
why_now: 2025-2026 solar installer bankruptcies (Sunnova, Mosaic, PosiGen) and the end of the residential solar credit produced the largest single wave of orphaned fixture filings ever recorded. 2018-2021 installs are now hitting their five-year lapse dates just as those homes come to market. Title agents are short-staffed and want to outsource curative work, and an LLM can read county index entries and bankruptcy docket text cheaply.
revenue_model: Flat fee of about $395-$900 per cleared file, contingent on clear-to-close. Agencies with volume pay $299/month plus a reduced per-file rate. White-label API for underwriters and closing software later.
non_obvious_insight: Half the 'problem liens' in solar-heavy counties are already legally dead, but the county index never shows lapse, so examiners treat a 2019 fixture filing as live forever. Clerks watch continuation filings come in, and most small installers never filed one. The work is proof of death, not payoff. Insiders also know the recorded 'notice of lease' is a different animal that never lapses, and that a clerk must record a debtor-filed termination on its face, since the office is ministerial.
first_30_days: Offer the first five files free to 3-5 independent title agencies in Phoenix, Tampa and Sacramento. Build the lapse calculator and county-index lookups for about 10 counties. Get one regional agent underwriter to accept a standard lapse-memo format. Then price at $495 per file and ask each agency for a testimonial and two referrals to listing agents.

title: Servicer-Funded Nonrenewal Rescue Agent for Homeowners
one_liner: When a homeowner's policy is nonrenewed, an agent contests the machine-made underwriting flag, documents mitigation and reshops 30 carriers plus the FAIR plan, paid by the mortgage servicer that would otherwise face a coverage lapse.
customer: Mortgage servicers and credit-union lenders pay per rescued loan; homeowners get the service free; a licensed partner agency earns placement commission.
problem: Homeowner nonrenewals are at records (a record 6,200 in New Mexico, Utah highest in 2025), premiums now rival mortgage payments, and California just passed three nonrenewal and claims bills (2026-09-03). Reinsurance is softening and cat bonds are at record issuance, yet primary policyholders see none of it. Carriers increasingly rely on aerial-imagery and AI scores (roof condition, overhanging trees, tarps) that are often wrong or fixable for a few hundred dollars, and homeowners have no one to contest a machine or work 30 quote portals.
solution: On a nonrenewal or a 25%+ renewal spike (detected from escrow data), a consumer-side agent gathers the stated reason, pulls imagery evidence where the state requires disclosure, and assembles a rebuttal or cure package (photos, contractor invoices, mitigation credits). In parallel it runs quotes across carrier and FAIR-plan portals acting as the user, and a licensed partner agency binds coverage. The servicer sees coverage status in a dashboard.
why_now: Nonrenewals are at records and states are adding rules. Softening reinsurance leaves carriers room to take documented risk back. Agentic browsers acting as the user now have appellate support (Ninth Circuit, 2026-08-04). Servicers face lapse, force-placed coverage and delinquency risk as insurance stress rises.
revenue_model: $100-250 per rescued loan from the servicer, 8-15% placement commission through the licensed agency, and contractor referral fees for cure work.
non_obvious_insight: The person in pain cannot pay, but the party whose collateral and cash flow depend on continuous coverage can. The counterparty is now a machine, so the rescue has to run at machine speed and machine cost: dollars per case for an agent versus hours for a human broker is what makes a $150 servicer fee profitable.
first_30_days: Pick one state (Colorado, Utah or Oklahoma). Partner with one credit union or regional servicer and run a free pilot on about 200 borrowers with nonrenewal notices, which they see in escrow analysis. Work the first 20 cases semi-manually with a licensed agency partner, track reinstatement and placement rates and cost per case, then quote the servicer a per-rescue fee.

title: Fake-Citation Triage for Defendants Facing Pro Se Filings
one_liner: A same-day report showing which citations in an opposing pro se filing are fake, misquoted or overruled, formatted as a court-ready exhibit for a motion to strike or for sanctions.
customer: Repeat defendants that get flooded with self-represented suits: landlord and property-management litigation groups, employment-defense boutiques, university and hospital counsel, insurer claims-litigation units, debt servicers, city attorney offices and municipal risk pools. Paid by the litigation budget owner.
problem: Charlotin's database holds about 2,095 AI-hallucination cases as of 28 Sep 2026, and 1,208 (58%) involve pro se litigants versus 829 involving lawyers. Pro se filers are immune to bar discipline, sanctions ($1,750 to $23,222) are slow and rare, and the defendant pays $300-600/hour of associate time to hand-check dozens of cites. Every hallucination-checker on the market is pitched to the lawyer who erred.
solution: Drag-and-drop a PDF. The tool extracts citations (open-source eyecite plus CourtListener), resolves each one, and flags nonexistent cases, quotes that do not appear in the opinion, wrong court or year, and negative treatment. Output is a two-page 'Citation Defect Declaration' plus a draft paragraph for a motion to strike or a Rule 11-type motion. Phase two hooks into the e-service email inbox so every incoming filing is screened automatically.
why_now: The volume of fabricated-citation filings is now measured in the thousands and judges have seen enough to act on them. Open case-law data (CourtListener) is now good enough that OpenAI built Astra for Law on it (17 Sep 2026), so the verification corpus is cheap for a small team.
revenue_model: $49-149 per filing report self-serve, or $1,500-5,000/month flat for repeat defendants with inbox integration. Upsell is drafting of the sanctions or strike motion at a fixed fee.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer everyone targets (the erring lawyer) has a small budget and an embarrassment problem. The money and standing sit with the counterparty, who pays hourly to verify someone else's junk and is the only actor who can turn a bad cite into leverage (strike, fee-shifting, vexatious-litigant designation).
first_30_days: Build on eyecite and the CourtListener API, then benchmark accuracy on 100 known cases from the Charlotin database as ground truth. Cold-email 30 landlord-tenant and employment-defense firms and 10 municipal risk pools, offering 10 free reports in exchange for permission to attach a report to a filing. Charge $99 per report after that and aim for 3-5 recurring accounts.

title: Child-in-the-Room Detector for Voice AI
one_liner: A tiny on-device SDK that infers from a few seconds of speech whether a speaker is likely a child, so voice assistants, cars, TVs and toys can drop into a safe policy tier without any login, camera or ID.
customer: OEMs of smart speakers, TVs and in-car assistants, voice-AI and companion app makers, and toy makers.
problem: Ambient voice AI serves shared households with no account or age signal. Laws and probes (CA SB 243, the FTC 6(b) inquiry, COPPA 'actual knowledge') create duties once a minor is present. Devices cannot tell a child from an adult, and asking kids to log in fails. The amended COPPA rule's biometric coverage makes storing voiceprints risky.
solution: An SDK under 5MB that classifies speaker age band (under 9, 9-15, adult) with calibrated confidence and an abstain option, using ephemeral features and never storing voiceprints. It returns a 'minor-likely' signal to trigger safe modes (topic limits, no romance roleplay, safe-messaging protocols) with audit logs. It is benchmarked publicly across accents and speech differences and fails safe by default.
why_now: Lawsuits and the FTC inquiry are pushing platforms to prove they detect minors, on-device speech encoders are good enough, and the brief flags a demand for privacy-preserving, non-ID age signals.
revenue_model: Per-device royalty of $0.10-0.50 or per-MAU pricing, plus paid integration and benchmark-certification services.
non_obvious_insight: For a voice product, the best age signal is the voice itself, with no ID, camera or login. The error costs are asymmetric: treating an adult as a child is cheap, the reverse is not, so 'fail safe' is the sales pitch.
first_30_days: Fine-tune an open speech encoder on licensed or consented child and adult speech corpora. Publish an open benchmark and baseline. Talk to 10 voice-AI and toy builders. Land 2 paid pilots at $3-5k each.

title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
customer: Adult heirs inheriting a home worth $300K-$1.5M where at least one wants to keep it. Distribution runs through probate attorneys and mediators. Capital comes from credit unions and community lenders.
problem: The default assumption is that inherited homes get sold and split. The recurring fight is one heir wanting to keep the house while the others want cash. The keeper often can't qualify for a cash-out refinance, because the estate isn't closed, income is thin, or no cash is on hand, so the outcome is a forced sale, a partition suit or a family break.
solution: A platform that (1) gets a neutral valuation (AVM plus appraiser) and a transparent buyout formula, (2) generates a sibling agreement covering the buyout, occupancy and carrying costs, with attorney review, and (3) structures financing: assume or continue the parent's existing low-rate first mortgage, plus a second lien or HELOC from a partner lender, closing when the estate can convey. Start as a licensed mortgage broker packaging these deals.
why_now: A large share of US mortgages carry rates near 3-4%, so the parent's loan is now valuable. Federal rules (Garn-St Germain and the CFPB successor-in-interest rules) generally let heirs keep servicing on an inherited mortgage without triggering due-on-sale. Gen X stands to inherit about $14T in the next decade (Cerulli), and market rates make cash-out refinancing unattractive.
revenue_model: Origination or broker fees of 1-1.5%, a $500-$1,500 platform fee for valuation and agreement docs, and referral or spread income from the second-lien partner.
non_obvious_insight: Locked-in low-rate mortgages turned the inherited house from an asset to liquidate into cheap capital to keep. The estate industry still defaults to 'sell', and lenders have no way to underwrite an heir with equity but no cash.
first_30_days: Pick one state. Sign five probate attorneys and one credit union. Get an MLO license or a broker partner. Handle three cases manually. Publish a free sibling-buyout calculator for estate forums and Facebook groups as the lead magnet.

title: Rent Seasonal Nitrate Treatment, Don't Build Plants
one_liner: Trailer-mounted nitrate-removal skids rented to small farm-belt utilities only for the 60-120 days a year when river or shallow-well nitrate spikes.
customer: Small and mid-size utilities (500-10,000 people) in Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Minnesota, Kansas and Wisconsin that draw from rivers or shallow aquifers. Systems with recent nitrate MCL violations are first. The utility pays, and state programs may help.
problem: More than 60M Americans are served from elevated-nitrate sources, and the 10 ppm limit dates from 1991. EPA's cancer review has stalled since 2023, and its research office is gone. Small rural systems bear treatment costs alone. A permanent $2-10M plant is out of reach for them, though the exceedance is seasonal.
solution: A fleet of containerized nitrate-selective ion-exchange skids sized 0.25-2 MGD. Include resin regeneration, brine logistics (the make-or-break piece, so pre-agree the disposal route with the wastewater plant or a hauler), operator training and remote monitoring. Priced as a seasonal service, per 1,000 gallons treated with a seasonal minimum. Start asset-light by leasing skids from an existing ion-exchange OEM.
why_now: Federal action on nitrate is stalled, so relief is not coming from Washington. Broad drought followed by heavy runoff swings nitrate hard. The FY2026 $7.2B SRF pool makes states receptive to flexible compliance solutions. The 10 ppm limit is still enforceable today.
revenue_model: Seasonal rental of $15-40k/month per skid plus per-gallon regeneration and brine fees, under 3-5 year master service agreements.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume compliance means permanent capital. But nitrate is a peak problem (Des Moines Water Works runs its removal plant only during high-nitrate stretches, from my background knowledge), so the winning model sells the peak, not the plant. A rental converts an unfundable capital project into a fundable operating line.
first_30_days: Pull three years of nitrate MCL violations from the public SDWIS database and build a list of 100 systems. Call five directly and through a state rural water association. Sign an MOU with one ion-exchange OEM for lease-back skids, and get one utility to agree to a paid pilot for spring 2027.

title: Fresh-Address Desk for Medicaid Plans
one_liner: Turn Title I front offices into a consent-based channel that keeps families on Medicaid, paid per household retained by health plans and hospitals, with a revenue share to the school.
customer: Medicaid managed care plans (member retention and quality-bonus teams) and nonprofit hospitals with community-benefit budgets. Principals and PTAs are the channel partners and receive a revenue share. They do not pay.
problem: Six-month renewals and work-requirement paperwork are scheduled to hit expansion-adult Medicaid enrollees in 2027. Plans lose members when renewal mail goes to old addresses and phone numbers, and their call-center contact rates are dismal. Kids often lose coverage in the household churn even when they stay eligible. Plans cannot reach the families who most need help, and the parent hears the plan's mail as junk.
solution: A text-first, home-language 'update your info and check your renewal' flow built into the school's existing August packet and registration. A part-time parent-liaison 'benefits desk' sits in the front office a few hours a week. Data goes to a plan only with a signed opt-in parent consent, not under FERPA directory information. Plans pay a fee per verified address or phone update and per completed renewal. About 30 percent of the revenue goes to a school-controlled discretionary fund. The same desk later handles other bounty-paying programs: utility low-income enrollment, Lifeline phone and internet plans, Summer EBT, and vision and dental follow-up.
why_now: Under the 2025 budget reconciliation law, expansion-adult redeterminations move to every 6 months after the end of 2026 and work requirements begin in 2027, unless states get a delay. The post-COVID Medicaid unwinding showed that most coverage losses were procedural. Principals are also hungry for discretionary dollars after the 2025 federal freezes and cancelled school-mental-health grants.
revenue_model: Per-household bounty of roughly $25 to $75 for a verified update or completed renewal. Plans also pay an annual per-school or per-region program fee. Optional add-on bounties from utilities and phone carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The freshest address and phone database of low-income families is not held by any agency. It is held by the school secretary, who re-verifies it every August because busing, lunch and emergency cards depend on it. Families ignore the plan's letters but answer the office they trust. Principals will only say yes if the money flows back to the school and consent is explicit, and that design is the moat.
first_30_days: Pick one state and call the community-engagement or quality director at two or three Medicaid plans. Offer a 90-day pilot in 3 schools whose principals you already know, priced per verified update. Build it with Twilio and a bilingual part-timer, and use a hashed list-match to show how many of a plan's returned-mail members appear in school records. Have the principal co-sign a one-page consent form that PTA volunteers can hand out.

title: Toddler Talk: Voice-Based Developmental Screening
one_liner: A phone-recorded three-minute parent-child talk sample plus automated screening workflow that helps pediatric practices catch speech and developmental delays earlier and capture reimbursement.
customer: Pediatric practices and health systems (developmental screening is billable under CPT 96110), Early Intervention programs and Medicaid managed care plans.
problem: Speech-language delay is a very common developmental issue, but screening relies on parent questionnaires with modest sensitivity, practices under-screen and Early Intervention waitlists are long. Kids are referred late.
solution: Phase 1 (no diagnostic claims) is a text-based well-visit screening workflow that increases completion and billing capture and collects consented audio. Phase 2 adds speech models that estimate vocabulary diversity, word combinations and turn-taking latency, giving clinicians a triage report. Phase 3 is a validated FDA pathway.
why_now: Speech models now handle child speech far better than before. Developmental screening is a CMS Child Core Set quality measure (from memory), so Medicaid plans pay for completion. Multimodal models make sample-based scoring feasible.
revenue_model: Per-screen fee or per-provider subscription ($200-500 a month), plus quality-improvement contracts with Medicaid plans, and later a per-report fee.
non_obvious_insight: Parents already record toddlers constantly. The bottleneck is not detection technology but screening completion and triage, so the winning move is to attach to the reimbursed screening code and Medicaid quality measures first and upgrade the signal later.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 independent pediatric practices through a developmental-behavioral pediatrician advisor. Run a 60-day free text-intake screening pilot. Capture consented audio for retrospective validation. Pitch one Medicaid plan's quality team on completion-rate lift.

title: Remote-Piloted Care Robots: Labor by Teleoperation
one_liner: Mobile manipulators supervised by remote pilots handle non-clinical night-shift chores in memory care, importing labor by bandwidth instead of visa.
customer: Memory-care and assisted-living operators (night and evening shifts), later affluent solo agers at home. The buyer is the operations executive with a labor budget.
problem: Night ratios of about 1:20 mean chores (water rounds, linen, trash, fetching supplies) compete with clinical rounds. Every open aide slot costs $45-60k with overtime. The 2026 visa pause closes the foreign-labor route.
solution: Off-the-shelf mobile manipulators (a Hello Robot Stretch-class robot, about $25k, and later humanoids) supervised by a bilingual remote pilot network trained on non-clinical tasks, with one pilot overseeing 3-4 robots. The first product is a night-shift runner: water and linen rounds, trash, fetch, room tidy, and a face-and-voice response to call lights that routes to a human aide. No lifting of residents and no clinical tasks.
why_now: Consumer humanoids with human-teleop fallback (1X's NEO opened preorders in late 2025), cheap mobile manipulators and vision-language-action models make assisted autonomy feasible in 2026. Wisconsin nursing homes' failed overseas-labor plan shows demand for labor by any route.
revenue_model: Robot-as-a-service at about $4,500 a month per robot for 12 hours a day (roughly $12-15 an hour against a $28-35 loaded aide cost), plus implementation fees.
non_obvious_insight: The moat is the pilot network, the safety case and the ops playbook, not the hardware. Teleoperation turns overseas labor into a service delivered without a visa, and a human-in-the-loop model works long before full autonomy.
first_30_days: Lease two Stretch-class robots and recruit six pilots from a Manila BPO. Run a free two-week night-shift pilot in one memory-care community, log chores and aide-minutes saved, and collect LOIs.

title: Voucher Lease-Up Desk for Soft Markets
one_liner: An ops service that gets units voucher-ready and through housing-authority inspection and paperwork in days, turning Section 8 from a hassle into the cheapest demand source in a soft market.
customer: Mid-size multifamily operators (300-5,000 units) in soft Sun Belt markets with high concessions, with housing authorities and mobility nonprofits as secondary payers.
problem: Apartment List shows 7.0% vacancy, 34 days to lease (longest September since 2019) and concessions on 15.8% of stabilized units (Austin 37%). Yet many operators still avoid Housing Choice Voucher applicants because inspection scheduling and contract paperwork can stretch weeks, costing roughly $300+ of rent a week on a $1,388 median unit. Voucher holders, meanwhile, fail to find units.
solution: A virtual pre-inspection app that walks site staff through HUD's NSPIRE-based checklist with photos so units pass first time. It automates the tenancy-approval and contract packet and tracks status across 50-100 local housing authorities, checks rent-reasonableness and payment standards before pricing, and publishes a live 'voucher-ready units' feed to caseworkers.
why_now: Time-to-lease is at a multi-year high and concessions are replacing rent growth, so landlords will trade a small admin burden for near-guaranteed rent. Authority inspections have moved to one federal standard, which a checklist app can encode.
revenue_model: $350-600 per successful voucher lease-up (against a $1,400 month of vacancy) or $1.50 per unit per month subscription, plus contracts with authorities and mobility programs.
non_obvious_insight: Operators treat vouchers as a risk problem when it is a cycle-time problem, measured in days, which is exactly what a 34-day-to-lease market prices. Government pays most of the rent, so the lowest-CAC tenant class is being left on the table. Housing-authority funding stress is the main risk, so sell to authorities with reserves and use source-of-income laws as a second wedge.
first_30_days: Pick two metros. Call 20 regional managers and offer a free pre-inspection pilot on 10 vacant units. Partner with two authority landlord-liaison offices and one mobility nonprofit. Charge only per lease-up once the unit is under contract with the authority.

title: Family Continuity Kit for Mixed-Status Households
one_liner: A done-with-you, notarized emergency-care package (standby guardianship, power of attorney, school and medical authorizations, wallet card and check-in alerts) for parents who could be detained without notice.
customer: Immigrant parents in mixed-status families, reached through trusted messengers such as churches, consulates, unions, clinics and schools. Co-payers: cities, counties and foundations funding preparedness, and employers in agriculture, meatpacking and hospitality. Price $49 to $149 per family, sliding scale.
problem: ICE issued Directive 11064.4 in July 2025 telling officers not to unnecessarily infringe parents' rights, but children still land in limbo when a parent is detained. The legal tools (standby guardianship, power of attorney, medical consent) are known, and nonprofits such as CLINIC and ILRC publish free guides. Execution is the bottleneck: state-specific forms, two-parent signatures, witnesses, a notary, and getting copies to the right person. California updated its guardianship rules in 2026, and city offices such as Chicago's 40th Ward publish emergency-plan guidance, which shows demand.
solution: A Spanish-first, WhatsApp-friendly workflow that interviews the parent, auto-fills the state's forms, and completes them through remote online notarization or notary-and-witness events at churches and clinics. Each family gets a wallet card with a QR code giving the designated caregiver instant access to the documents, plus school, bank and medical authorizations. Optional check-in alerts notify the caregiver and a legal-aid hotline if a parent misses a check-in. A caregiver checklist explains the first 72 hours. The forms are reviewed by legal-aid partners, and the app never collects immigration status.
why_now: Enforcement is at historically high levels in 2025 to 2026, and local governments are publishing family preparedness plans and updating guardianship law. Remote online notarization is available in most states, and messaging-app workflows reach families where they already are. Municipal and foundation budgets for know-your-rights work exist now.
revenue_model: $49 to $149 per family on a sliding scale. Municipal and county contracts to buy kits for residents ($25 to $40 each). Foundation grants. Union or employer benefit at about $5 per employee per year. Licensing to legal-aid organizations that lack completion capacity.
non_obvious_insight: For many immigrant families the highest-consequence legal document is not about immigration at all. It is a twenty-minute notarized form that keeps a child out of the foster system. Free guides exist but completion is low because the burden is witnesses, notaries, state variations and sharing, which can be productized. Payers exist beyond the family, since cities and foundations would rather fund kits than emergency foster placements.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a clear standby-guardianship statute. Have a legal-aid organization review the forms to avoid unauthorized-practice-of-law problems. Run notary-and-witness events at three churches or clinics and measure cost per completed family. Build the Spanish WhatsApp flow and printed wallet card, and design privacy so nothing about status is stored. Pitch one alderman's or county commissioner's office for a paid pilot of 500 kits.

title: Contingency Subrogation Forensics for Robot Accidents
one_liner: CCC-for-robots: a forensic recovery shop that turns warehouse-robot, AV and drone logs into fault-apportioned recovery demands for the insurers who already paid the claim.
customer: Subrogation units and TPAs at mid-size commercial P&C carriers, warehouse-focused MGAs, and brokers serving 3PLs and logistics parks.
problem: Robots damage racking, inventory, vehicles and people, and the insurer pays first, often under a policy never rated for robots. Recovery depends on whether the hardware, the model, the integrator's configuration, the operator's procedure or maintenance failed. The evidence sits in vendor-controlled logs and cloud consoles that get purged, and vendor contracts cap liability and force arbitration. Adjusters do not know what to ask for or how fast.
solution: A standard 72-hour evidence-preservation and vendor data-request package. Log parsers for the export formats of 3-5 common AMR, AGV, forklift and robotaxi platforms. A reconstruction timeline. A fault-apportionment matrix (OEM, integrator, operator, maintainer, site) with contract-cap analysis, plus a demand package addressed to the vendor's insurer.
why_now: Warehouse robot fleets, many of them imported, are scaling faster than underwriters' understanding, and trade press says insurers are unprepared. Robotaxi fleets are expanding across US cities in 2026. Carriers adding AI exclusions to GL, E&O and EPLI make 'which policy pays' a live dispute, which raises the value of recovering the loss from someone else. Claims from 2024-25 deployments are now maturing into subrogation files.
revenue_model: $3-8k flat fee per file plus 15-25% contingency on recoveries above a threshold. Later, annual retainers with carriers and a licensed evidence-request tool for adjusters.
non_obvious_insight: The first real price of AI and robot liability will be set in recovery negotiations, not in underwriting. Whoever standardises how blame is split between OEM, integrator and operator, and holds the resulting loss-cost data, becomes the rating bureau, as CCC and Verisk did in auto. The bottleneck is evidence access and speed, not legal theory.
first_30_days: Email 30 subrogation managers and TPAs offering a free reconstruction and recovery memo on one closed robot or AV claim within 10 days. Bring on an ex-robotics field-service engineer and subrogation counsel on a retainer. Write the preservation-letter pack. Aim for 2 paid files by day 60.

title: Scrap-to-Tab: Supply-House Credit for Trade Scrap
one_liner: A weekly scrap-and-refrigerant buy-back inside independent HVAC, plumbing and electrical supply houses that pays contractors in credit against their supply-house tab.
customer: Independent supply houses (channel, and they benefit from lower receivables) and their solo-to-10-tech contractor accounts. Downstream buyers are scrap mills, refrigerant reclaimers and rare-earth/copper processors.
problem: Small trades are cash-starved: 1 in 5 subs waits 60+ days to be paid, and residential HVAC shipments fell 25-50% in 2025 with equipment prices about 40% above 2020. Techs burn hours hauling old coils and copper to yards, or leave value in the dumpster. Supply houses carry the credit risk on 30-60 day terms.
solution: At the counter: sorted bins, a certified scale and basic grading. Contractors drop copper, brass, aluminum coil, old compressors/motors and recovered refrigerant (handled via a licensed reclaimer). Credit posts to their account, or cash is paid minus a small fee. We settle with the supply house in cash monthly, which cuts its receivables, and sell graded loads. Later add a bounty for magnet-bearing inverter compressors and motors, sold to rare-earth recyclers.
why_now: The HFC phase-down keeps cutting virgin refrigerant, making recovered gas strategic. The Aug 2026 BIS rule shows scrap is now a national-security asset and 'may add materials'. Hyperscalers are pulling rare earths out of waste streams. The HVAC trough is squeezing small-shop cash.
revenue_model: 10-20% spread on scrap; per-pound fee on refrigerant; supply-house sponsorship; rare-earth magnet bounty.
non_obvious_insight: The supply counter is the only place every small trade shows up weekly, it already extends credit, and it is a natural sorting checkpoint. Scrap value paid as tab credit is working capital the supply house wants (lower receivables) and contractors value more than yard cash.
first_30_days: Sign two independent supply houses in one metro. Place a scale and six bins. Buy at about 85% of local yard price for 30 days, then sell to a yard and a reclaimer. Measure pounds per week and receivables reduction, and pitch other houses on days-sales-outstanding improvement.

title: Guest-Funded Wildfire Hardening for Vacation Rentals
one_liner: An opt-in per-night 'fire-safe stay' fee that lets guests pay down the ember-proofing of the vacation homes they rent, unlocking insurance credits and renewals for owners who cannot afford the retrofit.
customer: Owners and property managers of vacation rentals and cabins in wildfire-exposed resort towns (Lake Tahoe/Truckee, Big Bear, Mammoth, Idyllwild, Estes Park, Ruidoso, Gatlinburg, Sunriver) facing nonrenewals or multiples of prior premiums. Insurers writing in distressed ZIPs are a secondary payer for leads.
problem: Retrofit baselines run $8K-25K while insurer discounts are only 5-35%, so owners cannot front the cash and the credit is unclaimable in practice. Short-term rentals are the least tolerated use for carriers. Owners are dropped over aerial-imagery roof photos and then have to prove their case. Yet these homes throw off daily cash flow, and their occupants are unfamiliar visitors with the highest life-safety exposure.
solution: An opt-in $3-6 per night fee at checkout (direct-booking sites and partner property managers) pools into a retrofit financing note for that specific house. Vetted crews install ember-resistant vents, roof and gutter fixes and 5-foot-zone clearing to the IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home standard. We build a time-stamped evidence pack (photos, receipts, certificate) and file it with the insurer under the new mitigation-credit and dispute rules. Guests see a public 'hardened home' badge. Owner pays nothing up front, and the fee stream repays the financier over 3-5 years.
why_now: Rules now force insurers to credit and explain: Colorado HB25-1182 has applied since 1 July 2026 (score disclosure, documented-mitigation credit, appeal) and California AB 75 (notice, photo copies, remediation window) went operative 1 July 2026. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington, signaling national scale. California launched a Safe Homes Grant and a revolving loan program. An FTC all-in-pricing rule for short-term lodging (effective May 2025) makes an opt-in structure the clean design.
revenue_model: 15-20% take of the surcharge flow, financing spread on the retrofit note, 3-5% contractor referral fee, and an insurer or MGA lead fee per credited policy or renewal.
non_obvious_insight: A vacation rental is the rare residential asset with a daily, price-insensitive cash stream that can service a retrofit loan, and guests are exactly the people the hardening protects. That aligns payer and beneficiary. Insurers hate short-term rentals most, so documented hardening changes the underwriting conversation where it matters most.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 owners through Big Bear and Truckee property managers. Get one local roofer or vent installer to give fixed-price bids. Add the opt-in fee line through an existing direct-booking tool (Hospitable, OwnerRez or Lodgify style widgets) and measure guest opt-in rate. Line up a $100-250K revenue-based note from a small local lender or angel. File the first evidence packs with two carriers.

title: Polling-Agent Payroll With Proof-of-Presence Release
one_liner: Pay each party or observer polling-unit agent directly, releasing money only after a geo-fenced arrival selfie and a result-sheet photo, so nothing gets skimmed on the way down.
customer: Election observer NGOs and civic groups (donor-funded, need audit trails) first. Then campaign directorates of governorship, National Assembly and state assembly candidates across parties. Later, any organisation paying temporary field staff.
problem: Election day is Nigeria's biggest one-day distribution of small payments. Agent allowances travel as lump sums from state to LGA to ward to polling-unit coordinators. Each layer keeps a cut, so a N20k allocation often reaches the agent as N5k. Agents then no-show, or get bought by the other side. Campaign directors know this leakage exists but have no proof and no tool. Since the 2023 cash scarcity, everything has been done by ad-hoc bank transfers and screenshots.
solution: A WhatsApp, USSD and light-Android flow. The party or NGO uploads its INEC-submitted agent list. Each agent gets a wallet or bank payout. Payment is released in tranches: 50% on a geo-fenced 7:30am arrival check-in, 50% on upload of the EC8A result-sheet photo. A coordinator dashboard shows attendance heat-maps and unpaid or unresponsive units in real time. Payments are for presence and documentation only, never for outcomes. Amounts are capped and pre-approved, and a spend report is produced for Electoral Act limits. The platform is strictly non-partisan and serves any party on identical terms.
why_now: INEC has fixed the presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027 and the governorship and state assembly polls for 6 February 2027. Parties must submit polling-agent names by 10 December 2026 and 6 January 2027. The campaign season is open now, with the Electoral Act 2026 in force. Nigeria has roughly 177,000 polling units, and every serious party wants an agent in each. LLM-based photo checks and cheap bulk-payout APIs (Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify transfers) make a small team viable. The deadline forces a fast pilot.
revenue_model: 2-3% fee on disbursed allowances, plus a per-agent onboarding fee of about N300-500. Campaigns and NGOs pay a flat SaaS fee for the dashboard and audit pack. Float on pre-funded wallets adds a small yield. After the elections, the same engine is resold as conditional-release payroll for temporary field workers: brand activations, survey and census enumerators, NGO vaccination and outreach drives.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer does not want digital payments. The buyer wants proof that the last person in a 5-layer cash chain actually showed up and got paid. Coordinators lose money to leakage, and that gives campaign principals a reason to bypass the middle layers. The wedge is fraud reduction, not fintech. A conditional-release payment is also more valuable as a workforce-verification product than as a payment product.
first_30_days: Build the check-in and photo flow on top of an existing payout API. Offer it free to one observer NGO or a single state-assembly campaign for a live Ekiti, Osun or by-election dry run, plus a paid pilot for a governorship candidate. Recruit 5 ward coordinators and get 500 agents paid in the first test. Approach NGO election-observation networks and donor programme officers, who already need audit trails. Get written non-partisan and INEC-compliance opinions from a lawyer before the first party contract. Price the first campaign at cost to get case studies.

title: Flooded Homeowners Meet Wetland Mitigation Buyers
one_liner: Match repeatedly flooded homeowners who want out with wetland and stream mitigation bankers who need floodplain land and can pay faster than federal buyouts.
customer: Compensatory-mitigation bankers, in-lieu-fee programs and land trusts (acquisition fee), counties and cities with repetitive-loss properties (program-management contracts), and homeowners (free, receive offers).
problem: Federal buyouts take years, and funding has become unreliable since the 2025 cancellation of BRIC and subsequent court fights. Meanwhile flood insurance premiums keep rising under Risk Rating 2.0 and repeat-flood homes are hard to sell. Mitigation bankers must buy contiguous floodplain and riparian land to earn Clean Water Act credits but usually source rural farmland by landman. They do not see suburban stream corridors lined with flooded homes as inventory.
solution: Screen NFIP repetitive-loss data, lidar and flood models and the RIBITS bank and credit ledger to find stream reaches where clusters of repeat-flood parcels adjoin high-credit-price watersheds. Run homeowner outreach and assemble willing sellers into a single package for a banker or land trust. The homes are demolished and the floodplain restored, with credits sold to permit-seeking developers and transport agencies.
why_now: Federal buyout money is slow and unpredictable, insurance repricing keeps rising, and data-center, industrial and transport permitting is driving demand for Section 404 mitigation credits. Public flood, lidar and ledger data make cluster screening possible for a small team.
revenue_model: Success fee of 2% to 3% of purchase price or $10k to $25k per assembled cluster (via a licensed real-estate partner), $2k to $5k a month screening subscription for bankers, and $50k to $150k municipal program-management contracts.
non_obvious_insight: A chain of flooded houses is exactly the restoration real estate a mitigation banker cannot otherwise get, and the funder of last resort can be a regulated compliance market rather than the taxpayer. This is a Clean Water Act compliance market, not a voluntary carbon-style offset.
first_30_days: Map 50 candidate reaches from public repetitive-loss, lidar and RIBITS data. Call 10 bankers and land trusts with a shopping list. Mail 200 homeowners on one reach. Sign a pilot with one banker and one county for program management.

title: Sell Heat Pumps to Health Plans
one_liner: Sell home electrification to Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans as a cost-of-care reduction instead of selling it to homeowners as a climate upgrade.
customer: Medicaid managed-care organizations, Medicare Advantage plans (supplemental benefits) and nonprofit hospital community-benefit budgets. They pay per completed install, plus an outcome bonus.
problem: The 25C credit ended 12/31/2025, homeowners face ~$9,000 heat pump quotes, and HEAR rebates roll out unevenly by state. Meanwhile health plans pay for asthma and COPD ER visits, heat illness and gas-stove-related respiratory events that cost thousands per admission.
solution: A 'clinical electrification program in a box'. Claims data finds members with asthma, COPD or heat vulnerability. A vetted contractor network installs a heat pump, heat pump water heater or induction cooktop. The program stacks HEAR/HOMES rebates so the plan pays only the gap, tracks ER visits and medication use, and reports ROI to the plan. Billing runs through Medicaid health-related-social-needs and in-lieu-of-service pathways or MA supplemental benefits.
why_now: Some state Medicaid waivers (Oregon's climate-device benefit) and MA plans already pay for air conditioners and air filtration. $8.8B of HEAR/HOMES money needs matching demand. Federal homeowner credits are gone, so the old buyer has weakened.
revenue_model: $2-6k net per install paid by the plan after rebate stacking, a platform fee, contractor take-rate, and outcome-based bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders keep trying to improve the homeowner's payback. The payer with the fastest ROI is the one who pays for ambulances. Health plans have budget lines, claims data to find the right homes, and no need for a 10-year payback.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a Medicaid climate-device benefit or a Southwest MA plan. Find two MCO community-health leads. Build claims-based targeting analytics. Run a 25-home pilot with one contractor using existing HEAR or utility rebates, and write a one-page ROI memo from baseline ER usage.

title: Outpatient Parvo Kits for Shelters and Low-Cost Clinics
one_liner: Parvo is treated as inpatient-only, but a standardized ambulatory protocol in a box plus remote nurse monitoring can cut cost per case dramatically for shelters that otherwise euthanize.
customer: Municipal animal services, shelters and spay-neuter/low-cost clinics. Secondary: urgent-care clinics serving low-income clients.
problem: Inpatient parvo care often costs thousands of dollars, so shelters and owners choose euthanasia, and vets suffer moral distress. The briefing notes vet care is nearly half of pet-cost inflation since 2019 and that clinicians routinely alter plans for money. The outpatient protocols exist (Colorado State published one in 2017 reporting survival in the range of hospitalization; re-verify in the pilot) but only as PDFs, not as a product with logistics.
solution: A vet-signed kit per case (SC fluids, maropitant, antibiotics, syringes, nutrition support, dosing cards, video training) sold by a partner clinic-of-record. Twice-daily photo/video/weight/hydration logs are reviewed by an RVT desk with DVM sign-off, with hard escalation rules to inpatient transfer. A shared outcome registry proves results to funders. Extend to other ambulatory-able acute problems (uncomplicated gastroenteritis, SC-fluid CKD cats).
why_now: Access philanthropy just scaled (Duffield 2026-09-17; PetSmart Charities), and funders want cost-per-outcome evidence. Shelters are overcrowded and Texas transports have been slowed by screwworm restrictions. Remote VCPR rules are loosening piecemeal, and spectrum-of-care thinking is now mainstream.
revenue_model: $150-300 per case for kit plus monitoring, versus thousands for inpatient care. Annual shelter subscription ($2-5K) with usage tiers, often paid from grant dollars. Protocol licensing to low-cost clinic chains.
non_obvious_insight: The 'standard of care' for parvo is partly a business-model artifact: hospitals are paid to hospitalize. Nobody sells the cheaper protocol as a logistics-and-monitoring product, and the buyers (shelters, funders) are motivated by lives saved per dollar.
first_30_days: Partner with 3 shelters and one shelter-medicine vet. Assemble kits from wholesale distributors via the vet's prescriptions. Run 20 cases with structured data on survival, days to eating and cost. Apply for a $10K micro-grant to underwrite the pilot. Publish a one-page outcomes summary.

title: AI-Label Pre-Flight Before You Upload
one_liner: A 'spellcheck for platform AI labels' that predicts how each service will tag and treat a file before it goes live.
customer: Social video teams, agencies, MCNs, podcast networks, and labels or distributors delivering to several DSPs, all of whom use mixed tool chains.
problem: Every major platform now labels or penalizes AI content: YouTube auto-labels (May 27), TIDAL badges and demonetizes (Jul 15), Snapchat stopped recommending fully-AI Spotlight content (Jul 31), and Spotify excludes AI persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11). Labels can be triggered by markers in any single asset, such as one generative b-roll clip or an AI retouch, and rules differ per platform. Teams cannot predict outcomes.
solution: Upload the final export or stem set. The tool reads C2PA manifests, IPTC DigitalSourceType and XMP, runs public watermark verifiers where they exist, applies per-platform rule tables, and predicts the label and monetization outcome per service. It points to the timeline segments or assets that triggered it, drafts accurate disclosure text, and logs the result. It recommends fixes such as re-rendering a clip, and never strips manifests. Ships as plugins for Premiere, Resolve and Frame.io plus an API for DAM systems.
why_now: Platform penalties for AI labeling only became real between May and Aug 2026, and the rules differ across services. Content Credentials adoption (TikTok joined in Jul 2026) means more assets carry markers.
revenue_model: $49-499/month per team, an API at $0.02 per asset, and $2-10k/month enterprise plans.
non_obvious_insight: The market has focused on creating labels and detecting AI. Once labels carry monetization consequences, the demand is for predicting them, like SEO tools for policy. Honest teams with minor assistive AI, not cheats, are the buyers, and the product keeps disclosure accurate.
first_30_days: Build a parser on the open-source c2pa-rs library plus a rule table from published policies. Test it on 200 real videos. Offer 10 agencies a free label audit of their last 20 uploads and sell the first team plans.
